claims.text: The Enabling Act of 1933 was passed by the Reichstag on 23 March 1933 with a two-thirds majority. The Nazis and their ally the DNVP controlled well below two-thirds of the votes. The Communist delegates had been banned from participation. The Nazis used intimidation tactics, such as surrounding the Reichstag with SA members, to secure the necessary votes. The Nazis promised religious freedom protections to the Catholic Centre Party to secure the necessary votes. Only the Social Democratic Party (SPD) voted in opposition to the Enabling Act. The vote on the Enabling Act was 444 to 94. The Reichstag president Hermann Göring changed the rules of procedure to reduce the quorum required for constitutional amendments. Hermann Göring did not count the 81 absent Communist deputies when calculating the quorum. The quorum was lowered from 432 to 378. The Nazis used coercion, bribery, and manipulation of parliamentarians to ensure the bill's passage. The conservative parties were expected to support the Enabling Act. The Social Democrats and Communists opposed the Enabling Act. Communist and some Social Democrat deputies had already been arrested under the Reichstag Fire Decree before the vote.

claims.text: Murdering Europe's Jews became coordinated state policy around the time of the Wannsee Conference on 20 January 1942. The Wannsee Conference was convened by Reinhard Heydrich to coordinate anti-Jewish policy across German-occupied Europe. The Wannsee Conference formalized plans for the total eradication of the Jewish population of Europe. The Wannsee Conference marked the implementation of the Final Solution to the Jewish Question. Before the Wannsee Conference, killings were carried out by local initiatives such as Einsatzgruppen mass shootings and random violence. The Wannsee Conference represented the shift to a continent-wide, organized genocide involving deportations to extermination camps equipped with gas chambers. The majority of Holocaust killings were carried out in 1942. Over 3 million Jews were murdered in 1942. The number of Jews murdered in 1942 indicates the peak of the coordinated genocide. Hitler resolved to exterminate the Jews immediately around December 1941, following the failed offensive against Moscow. Hitler made a verbal declaration to Nazi officials on 12 December 1941 that the annihilation of the Jews must be the necessary consequence of the world war. The decision to exterminate the Jews was finalized shortly before the Wannsee Conference. Local violence and killings had been ongoing before early 1942. The coordinated state policy to murder all Jews across Europe was formalized and implemented starting in early 1942.
claims.reason: "Around the time of the failed offensive against Moscow in December 1941, Hitler resolved that the Jews of Europe were to be exterminated immediately." - Wannsee Conference formalized plans for total eradication and coordinated genocide began in 1942.
